# Issue 5: Chainsaw rule

## Outcome

A member who has not done the induction for a class-C tool, such as the chainsaw, cannot borrow it.
A member who has done the induction can.

## Requirements

- If the item is safety class C and the member's inductions do not include "C", the system shall refuse the loan with `ok: false`.
- If the loan is refused for a missing induction, the system shall give a reason that names the item and says an induction is needed.
- Where the item is safety class C and the member's inductions include "C", the system shall allow the loan when the item is in.
- While a member has no inductions, the system shall still allow class A and class B tools that are in.
- When a member with the "C" induction asks for a class-C tool that is out or in repair, the system shall still refuse it for that reason.

## Must not change

- `src/auth/` is not touched.
- Class A and class B tools keep their current rules: free tools go out, tools in repair or already out do not.
- The existing tests stay as they are.

## Out of scope

- Inductions for other classes (a "B" induction rule).
- How a member gets an induction, or recording one.
- The desk screens and server routes.

## Done when

- `bun run gate` exits 0.
- The new tests in `tests/items/borrow.test.ts` pass.

content.text: Spec and tests are written; now running the tests to confirm the new ones fail.

I wrote `specs/5/SPEC.md` and added five tests to `tests/items/borrow.test.ts`. I changed nothing under `src/`. `bun test tests` gives 13 passing and 2 failing. The two new tests that describe the missing behaviour fail, as intended.

The issue only says "chainsaw", so I read it as "class-C tools need the `C` induction". The chainsaw is the only class-C tool in the seed, and the seed members who have an induction hold `"C"`. If the rule should apply to the chainsaw by id instead, the spec needs changing.

The two failing tests:
- A member without the `C` induction cannot take the chainsaw (it is currently allowed).
- The refusal reason names the tool and mentions an induction.

The other three new tests already pass, as expected:
- An inducted member can take the chainsaw.
- An uninducted member can still take a class-B tool.
- An inducted member is still refused a chainsaw that is out or in repair.

They guard against over-blocking once the builder adds the rule. The spec has one requirement line for each of the five tests. I did not run `bun run gate`.
